newsitem.title: USA: Texas Instruments to unveil new chip Monday.
newsitem.headline: Texas Instruments to unveil new chip Monday.

text.p: Texas Instruments Inc said it will introduce on Monday a powerful new computer chip that can process 1.6 billion instructions per second.
Spokeswoman Karen Cook said the digital-signal processor has about 40 times the processing power of a comparable chip in an ordinary computer modem.
Texas Instruments shares were up 5-3/4 to 80-3/8 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
Digital signal processors, or DSPs, convert sights and sounds into digital computer language and are used in wireless phones, compact-disk players and other audiovisual equipment.
Cook said the chip does not move information faster, but instead transmits more information simultaneously.

The Dallas-based company has banked its future on semiconductors in general and DSPs in particular. It earlier this month annnounced it was selling its defense-electronics unit and its computer notebooks division as part of an effort to focus on the chip market.
Texas Instruments currently accounts for about 45 percent of the DSP market.
